newsitem.title: BELARUS: Switzerland, Austria freeze credit lines to Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland, Austria freeze credit lines to Belarus.

text.p: Switzerland and Austria have joined Germany in freezing credit lines to Belarus, which owed $18.1 million on foreign credits as of May 1, an economy ministry official said on Wednesday.
"Foreign credits are wasted in Belarus. On the whole it is a good thing that European states have frozen their credit lines this year," said the official, who asked not to be named.

Foreign credits to Belarus stood at $143 million last year from $367 million the previous year. "Of unused credits in open credit lines, Germany has frozen $66 million, Austria $470 million and Switzerland $7 million," he said in an interview.
Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, who is not keen on introducing radical market reform to his struggling former Soviet republic, has said it does not need foreign credits.

An economy ministry document showed that enterprises which received credits under government guarantee from the International Monetary Fund had asked the authorities to extend their repayment deadline by four or five years from 1998.

The document, obtained by Reuters, showed that of $199.7 million received to restructure enterprises, non-payments included $10 million from the Minsk tractor factory and $2 million from the October Revolution plant.
The IMF paid a first, $98 million tranche of a systemic transformation facility to Belarus in July 1993 and a second worth $101.7 million in February 1995.

An IMF stand-by deal worth $250 million was agreed in Belarus in September 1995 but frozen in January 1996 pending faster reforms. Minsk received $70 million of the cash to cover currency support and the budget deficit.
